title: Air-fryer kofta
subtitle: Spiced lamb mince shaped on skewers and air-fried until charred.
excerpt: Minced lamb seasoned with cumin, coriander, onion, and chilli, shaped around skewers and cooked in the air fryer until browned outside and still juicy within. Ready in 20 minutes. Serves four.
sourceNotes: Kofta refers to minced meat shaped around a skewer and grilled over charcoal across Middle Eastern, South Asian, and Eastern European cooking traditions. This air-fryer version achieves a similar surface char without a grill.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze shaped raw kofta on a tray, then transfer to bags. Cook from frozen at 200°C for 16-18 minutes.
recipe.batchNotes: Double easily. Chill for 30 minutes so they hold shape on the skewer.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Shape and refrigerate for up to 24 hours before cooking.

content.text: Kofta needs fat in the mix to stay juicy: lamb mince at 20% fat is ideal. Too lean and the kofta falls apart on the skewer and dries out quickly. Mix firmly ,  the protein in the meat acts as a binder ,  and chill for 30 minutes before cooking so they hold their shape.

Grate {{onion}} onion and squeeze the moisture out firmly in a clean cloth or with your hands. Combine {{lamb-mince}} of lamb mince with the squeezed onion, {{garlic}} of grated garlic, {{cumin-ground}} of cumin, {{garam-masala}} of garam masala, {{chilli-powder}} of chilli powder, and {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt. Mix with your hands for 2 minutes until the mixture feels sticky and holds together. Divide into 8 portions and shape each around a flat metal or pre-soaked wooden skewer, pressing firmly. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Preheat the air fryer to 200°C. Spray the kofta lightly with cooking oil and cook for 6 minutes, turn, and cook for a further 4-6 minutes until browned and cooked through.

items.cause: Meat not mixed firmly, or too much moisture from the onion.
items.fix: Mix the meat aggressively for 2 full minutes. Squeeze every drop of moisture from the grated onion before mixing.
Use lamb mince with at least 20% fat. Lean mince makes kofta that is tight and dry rather than juicy.

items.cause: Skewer too thick or pieces too large.
items.fix: Keep the kofta to about 3 cm diameter and 12 cm long. Thicker pieces take longer to cook through.

content.text: Kofta from the air fryer is a quick weeknight dinner. Serve in flatbreads with sliced tomato, onion, and yoghurt, or over rice with a herb salad. The same mix makes good meatballs for pasta if you drop the skewers and form into rounds instead.
